nodes.label: dcmjs Rewrite — Visibility & Communication Report (2026-07-15, Abigail ↔ Jarkko review loop)
nodes.author: Claude (Fable)
nodes.rationale: Pre-digests the 28 open PRs on awatson1978/dcmjs: architecture, computed dependency graph, three call chains, timeline, two debt ledgers, decision skeleton, PR cards, reading order. 1,422 tests, 99.8% green on both read cores. Prepared at Jarkko Kemppainen's request; the IDesign projection is the report's interpretation, not the repo's vocabulary.

nodes.label: Haiku thesis: 'One contract; three sources; one truth. Thirteen small steps made the mountain reviewable. Every debt is written down — nothing hides.'
nodes.rationale: The whole report compressed into three lines; everything else is presented as evidence for these claims. UC-2 (slice G, PR #27) is the thesis expressed as a test: if any of the 30 fixtures naturalizes differently from any source, the suite fails.

nodes.label: 15-verb event-stream contract band (versioned CONTRACT_VERSION, normative, conformance-tested)
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing element of the architecture: sources emit a 15-vocabulary-verb contract with balanced nesting invariants and loss preservation; listeners consume it with zero knowledge of where bytes came from. Keystone decision D1: settle the vocabulary once and every reader, writer, and listener becomes a bounded component.

nodes.label: IDesign layer model projection of the four specified layers (sources → event stream → listeners/writers → naturalized metadata)
nodes.rationale: One manager orchestrates; every arrow is a permitted call direction; nothing calls upward. decodeCore sits inside ResourceAccess — byte→value translation deliberately consolidated to one place (R3) so the lazy reader and the streaming source cannot silently diverge. Explicitly flagged as the report's interpretation, to be challenged in review.

nodes.label: The legacy island: pre-contract read path (AsyncDicomReader, 774 loc) that bypasses the contract
nodes.rationale: 'The red island is the honest part': AsyncDicomReader runs its own header/element loop on the old listener vocabulary and never touches the contract. Frame-level pixel semantics live only here. Marked and deferred in writing (AD-2/AD-3, K7 assessment).

nodes.label: Dependency claim: the read side and the sink side share no imports — they meet only through emitted events at runtime
nodes.rationale: Every edge in the section-2 graph is a real import statement at the fable/event-stream tip. Source-independence is not a convention, it's the import graph: NaturalizedListener imports dictionaries and the push core, never a parser. One deliberate, decision-logged crossing exists (D15, the Part 10 writer).

nodes.label: Three defining call chains: UC-1 streaming read (bounded memory), UC-2 equivalence gate (three sources, one truth), UC-3 write path (no second encoder)
nodes.rationale: UC-1: events flow while chunks are still arriving; consumed chunks released fire-and-forget; backpressure (awaitDrain) travels backward at element boundaries; gates 1–7 in PR #42 prove event-for-event identity down to 1-byte chunks. UC-2: the architecture's thesis as a test (slice G, PR #27). UC-3: decision D15 — round-trip costs 36 lines because the proven encoder is reused; unedited elements pass through verbatim (zero-copy).

nodes.label: Act I — Rewrite the core (May 19 → Jun 28, PRs #21–#27)
nodes.rationale: Upstream fixes and pnpm workspaces; dicom-parser vendored as @dcmjs/parser with byte offsets; lazy read core + backpatching writer (R0–R7); docs site; then the event-stream contract, generators, naturalized model, and cross-source equivalence (slices A–G). Jun 10 cluster = lazy core landing (635 tests); Jun 28 = the entire event-stream architecture (1,128 tests).

nodes.label: Act II — External review folded in (Jul 3, PRs #28–#29)
nodes.rationale: Steve Pieper's architecture review captured as decisions D16–D25 with drafted responses — then D22 implemented: a machine-readable schema catalog with TypeScript and JSON-Schema projections generated from one source of truth.

nodes.label: Act III — Prove it with a sink (Jul 6, PR #30: @dcmjs/fhir)
nodes.rationale: DICOM → FHIR Patient + ImagingStudy (IHE MADO), built purely on the naturalized keyword API — the third independent consumer of the same model, zero DICOM parsing of its own. Proves the naturalized model supports consumers never imagined when the contract was written.

nodes.label: Act IV — Make it stream (Jul 6–7, PRs #31–#43, #44)
nodes.rationale: One shared decode core extracted, then fromPart10Stream built in 13 steps: chunked input → incremental FMI → body loop → undefined-length → streaming deflate → formal gates. #31–#36 behavior-neutral consolidation; #37–#43 one capability each. Jul 6 delivered all thirteen streaming steps in a single-session burst.

nodes.label: D12 — Loss preservation over policing
nodes.rationale: The stream emits every observed value regardless of declared VM; cardinality enforcement is a listener concern. This one rule is why three sources can naturalize identically (UC-2).

nodes.label: D15 — Reuse the proven encoder (Part 10 writer layers over canonical DicomDict.write)
nodes.rationale: Round-trip capability costs 36 lines because the proven encoder is reused rather than growing a second encoder; unedited elements pass through verbatim (zero-copy). This is the single deliberate import crossing the read/sink divide in the dependency graph.

nodes.label: D22 — One schema, three projections (normative rule catalog + TypeScript + JSON-Schema from one source)
nodes.rationale: The naturalized model's contract became machine-readable: a consumer's TypeScript compiler and an ajv validator now enforce the same rules, because both projections derive from one catalog, held together by CI freshness-and-agreement gates (which are load-bearing — see ED-5). ~75.5k of PR #29's lines are generated artifacts: regenerate-and-diff, don't read.

nodes.label: K7 — Evidence-based deferral of the AsyncDicomReader re-platform
nodes.rationale: Re-platforming AsyncDicomReader was assessed, two concrete breakage points documented (frame splitting, compressed-frame assembly), and the work deferred to 1.x — a written 'no' instead of a silent one (AD-2).

nodes.label: D16–D25 — Steve Pieper's external review, answered in writing
nodes.rationale: External review logged with drafted responses: byte-identity guarantees, naming (events → dicomEventStream, materialize → naturalize), a validation layer, and proposed slices H (conformance) and I (dicom-curate). Governance in action — external feedback becomes traceable decisions before any code is written. Reviewers should check D16–D25 against memory of Steve's actual comments; a mischaracterized review comment would hide here.

nodes.label: D0–D6, D13–D14 — Foundational decisions: decompose contract-first; push core + pull adapter + sync hot path; binary/FMI/provenance; ergonomics without lying
nodes.rationale: D0–D1: 'refactor all of it' against ~40 pages of specs split into dependency-ordered slices A–G, contract first. D2–D3: push/callback canonical with async-iterator on top; synchronous calls with async checkpoints keep the hot path allocation-free while giving backpressure at element boundaries. D4–D6: encapsulated pixel data as fragment sub-stream, FMI as bracketed leading sub-stream, optional sourceSpan byte ranges for provenance. D13–D14: Person Name proxies (.Alphabetic, string-coercion to raw PN); numbers exceeding double precision keep the raw source string alongside the decoded value.

nodes.label: OD-1–OD-4 — Decisions awaiting a human owner (not debt, but unowned risk)
nodes.rationale: All four flagged in the roadmap since 2026-06-10; none can be Fable's call. OD-1 scalar collapse (VM-driven value shapes — breaking, API-owner sign-off). OD-2 ISO_IR 192 normalize-on-read (changes byte-identical round-trip; standards posture). OD-3 binary values as zero-copy views by default (aliases caller's buffer — a footgun owners must accept knowingly). OD-4 public dict key format (public API contract; migration cost lands on users).

nodes.label: The 28-PR review structure: four serially-dependent stacks (A rewrite core #21–27, B architecture review & schema #28–29, C FHIR sink #30, D streaming #31–43) + meta umbrellas #1/#2/#5/#6/#44
nodes.rationale: 23 stacked steps, 4 umbrella views, 1 test report, between four integration branches. Umbrellas are windows, not work. Merge risk: stacks are serially dependent through the integration branches — if review rejects something in Stack A, every stack above it rebases; hence review bottom-up (A → B → C/D). The 16 closed PRs are fully accounted for: #7–#19 re-opened as #31–#43 for chronological numbering (identical diffs), one duplicate, one early merge, one re-created FHIR PR.

nodes.label: PR #22 — Offsets parser + lazy read/write core (R0–R7): 'the heart of the rewrite'
nodes.rationale: dicom-parser vendored as @dcmjs/parser (195 tests, byte spans on every element); LazyDicomReader deferring decode via getters; in-place backpatching and verbatim-byte passthrough on write; deflate-on-write; lazy core promoted to default. The old eager model decoded every element whether or not anyone asked; laziness plus offsets is what later makes streaming and byte-identity possible. 635 tests pass identically on both cores; parser benchmark ≈0.84× geomean vs. published dicom-parser.

nodes.label: PR #27 — Cross-source equivalence matrix, Part 10 writer & API polish (slices G/E2)
nodes.rationale: The 30-fixture matrix proving bytes, dicts, and DICOMweb JSON naturalize identically (UC-2); scale validation (100k-item sequences, 500-deep nesting); auto-detecting DicomEventStream.from(). 'The single best PR for did-the-AI-capture-sufficient-context — the equivalence matrix either holds or it doesn't.' 1,128 tests green. Slice G is the architectural thesis made testable.

nodes.label: PR #29 — D22 naturalized schema catalog (+76,504 lines, ~75.5k generated)
nodes.rationale: VM pattern parser, catalog generator, compiler-validated TypeScript projection, JSON-Schema 2020-12 projection, code-agreement gate against the fixture corpus, public dcmjs/schema subpath. Review the generator, the VM parser, and the agreement gate — don't read the generated files, regenerate and diff.

nodes.label: PR #30 — @dcmjs/fhir: naturalized DICOM → FHIR (toFhir), the third independent sink
nodes.rationale: Maps DICOM patient module → FHIR Patient (MR identifier, US Core extensions) and study/series/instance → ImagingStudy (IHE MADO, urn:dicom:uid). API: toFhir(), toBundle(), fromPart10(). Strict contract: absent elements omitted, unsupported versions throw, no invented IDs. Consumes only the naturalized keyword API — zero DICOM parsing of its own.

nodes.label: PR #42 — fromPart10Stream formal streaming gates 1–7: streaming ≡ buffered down to 1-byte chunks
nodes.rationale: Streaming ≡ buffered across a 29-fixture corpus at every granularity from whole-file to 1-byte chunks, plus backpressure and truncation gates (~110 gate tests). Also fixes per-fragment memory bounding and an FFFE-tag endianness regression that lost SQ content in Big Endian files. 'The difference between it-seems-to-work and a verifiable claim' — the review centerpiece for the whole stack; read the gate definitions, not the fixture output.

nodes.label: Suggested review path: plan docs first, then bottom-up A (#21–27) → B (#28–29) → C (#30) → D (#31–43) → evidence (#44) → debt ledgers
nodes.rationale: Ordered by the merge-risk argument (stacks serially dependent). Read CLAUDE_REFACTOR_PLAN.md and CLAUDE_REFACTOR_ANALYSIS.md first — they are the web every PR hangs from; validating them validates the AI's context. No single sitting bigger than one idea. Umbrellas #1/#2/#5/#6 are for browsing, not approving. The debt ledgers double as the post-merge work plan. The fastest way to validate captured context is to read the decisions, not the diffs.

nodes.label: Debt retired along the way (PAID ledger): five upstream bugs (#21), SplitDataView.consume bugs (#36), implicit-VR item-tag bug (#39), FFFE endianness regression (#42), delegation fallbacks removed (#34, #41)
nodes.rationale: Credited as evidence the review process finds real defects: SR template leak, sync/async charset divergence, missing UV → BigInt, async over-read past sentinel tags, Babel debt; three correlated consume-listener bugs found before streaming depended on them for memory accounting; a latent cross-path bug surfaced by equivalence testing (residual gap tracked as AD-1); the secretly-re-parse-everything paths are gone.

nodes.label: Stakeholder decision (2026-08-02): deprecate lazy parser — event stream gets 90% of benefit
nodes.rationale: Post-report stakeholder call (Jarkko loop): the lazy parser's remaining 10% benefit (byte-identity passthrough) isn't justified by its cost; eager becomes default engine again, lazy deprecated for removal next release, event stream is the strategic surface.
